correctness.rationale: The centered four-level vector has squared norm V=9pq/(p+q)-4 and energy B minus total optional-edge conductance. Equality forces all optional weights to vanish, and the leaf and first-hub eigenvector equations then force exactly the displayed weights. They are positive on the tree edges and sum to B. For an independent quotient check, put d=3pq/(p+q), a=3q/(p+q), b=3p/(p+q), c=d-1. The block-constant quotient has eigenvalues 0 and 1 from the constant and centered four-level vectors. Its trace is 4d-2 and the sum of its principal order-three minors is (p+q)abc=3d(d-1). Thus the other two roots have sum 4d-3 and product 3d(d-1), giving d and 3d-3, both greater than 1. The transverse eigenvalues are a and b, with multiplicities p-2 and q-2. When a transverse space is absent its corresponding inequality is automatic. Thus equality holds on the entire closed factor-two range including the boundary; outside it the forced candidate has an eigenvalue below the target, and a strict bound follows by compactness. Uniqueness concerns the conductances even if the eigenvalue is multiple.
residual_risks: The 529 recorded finite exact checks are not the proof for all side orders. No exact out-of-range augmented-graph optimum is claimed.

evidence: For d=3 and P=max(p,q), Q=min(p,q), set n=P+Q and k=(P-Q)/2 when n is even, (P-Q-1)/2 when n is odd. Richter–Rocha's cutoff is k=n/6 when n is even, (n-3)/6 when odd; both translate to P=2Q.

Their form (1) line embedding is constant on each leaf class, with unit changes along the three edge levels. Its variance is V. Form (2) gives tree variance P+4Q-4, which exceeds V by (P-2Q)^2/(P+Q) off the cutoff. The two values coincide at the cutoff; the comparison quadratic in Proposition 13's proof has a double root there.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known larger double-broom family contains the full claimed tree range, with the same transition and closed boundary, not just identical-size cliques or a single discrete example.

evidence: The tree line vector remains a feasible dual vector after adding any within-side leaf edges, whose endpoint distances in it are zero. It gives the same universal upper bound, whether or not it is optimal on the tree. Inside the closed range an optimal tree allocation extends with zero weights to attain the bound. Strict slack on each added edge forces its weight to be zero in every equality allocation, reducing uniqueness to the tree or to its leaf and hub equations. Outside the range an equality allocation would similarly reduce to a tree equality allocation, impossible because P+4Q-4>V.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This implication covers even asymmetric choices of optional edges and the strictness claim, not just the quoted tree case. The extension requires only feasibility of the existing line certificate and its zero length on added edges; a new outside-range augmented optimum would be a different claim.

evidence: The double star is the diameter-three double broom. Scaling its absolute algebraic connectivity from total weight n-1 to B gives the same fixed-budget problem. Sun et al.'s centered maximum-variance embedding is its dual at unit edge cost.

evidence: The priced asymmetric tree record gives a unique optimum at all bridge prices; at t=1 its balanced-branch weights are the frozen weights on the tree, and for P>2Q its budget-one value is 1/(P+4Q-4). The mirrored priced record overlaps only the balanced tree setting. The prior closed forms are stronger than finite numerical tables.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: An explicit existing formula specializes to the claimed exact tree values and weights. The published tree formula alone is not an exact table of arbitrary augmented-graph optima, and the frozen record makes no such calculation outside the range.

originality.rationale: The claimed closed threshold and tree optimum specialize prior double-broom results; the priced double-star catalog record also already gives the tree weights and uniqueness at unit bridge price. The arbitrary optional-edge extension, including strictness outside the range, follows directly from the known centered line embedding and standard complementary slackness because every added edge has length zero. The augmented-graph result need not be stated verbatim in the prior papers for the whole reviewed claim to follow. This is demonstrated prior implication, not failure to establish originality due to access limits.
residual_risks: Richter–Rocha's final journal version and Fiedler's primary full text were not recovered. The verdict uses the accessible author's exact formulas and embedding results plus the dual certificate, not a claim about wording in inaccessible versions.

value.rationale: The allocation question is natural and the short proof is useful exposition. As a proposed new result, however, the tree cutoff, values and rates are already obtained from stronger prior results. The only apparent scope increment consists of added edges on which the known optimal line certificate has coincident endpoints. Dual feasibility and strict slack then give exactly the claimed deletion, and the same slack reduces strictness to the known tree inequality. There is no surviving independently useful unknown invariant or boundary in the frozen claim. No repair is supplied: a new theorem about optimal use of optional edges or their exact value outside the factor-two range was not established here.
residual_risks: This rejects the scientific increment of the stated claim, not the mathematical correctness of its certificate or the value of pursuing a genuinely new out-of-range theorem.
